brief:
Amin Abu Rashed, secretary general of the Palestine Conference of Europeans-Netherlands, told Shehab Wire that Palestinian National Council elections represent a right, legitimacy, and popular will rather than mere procedural matters. He stressed that continuing appointment policies amounts to confiscating the people's will and contradicts foundational principles of democratic representation.

Abu Rashed argued that any leader unwilling to face the ballot box does not deserve to represent Palestinians, according to Shehab Wire. His remarks reflect ongoing tensions within Palestinian political circles over whether the National Council should be elected or appointed. The debate centers on competing visions of institutional legitimacy and democratic accountability within Palestinian governance structures.
